Worked example

Create a fictitious contract with a unique phrase that appears nowhere else in your test workspace. Upload it as a member of the legal team. Have a colleague with a sales-only account search for the phrase. Record the account, time and result so the vendor can reproduce what you saw.

Worksheet
CheckpointEvidence to collect
Upload and retrievalRecord which team can retrieve the contract, its filename and generated summaries. Repeat after removing the uploader’s access.
Processing and logsAsk the vendor to trace the request ID through its model provider, search index and support logs. Record who can inspect each copy.
DeletionDelete the test file and repeat the search. Ask when embeddings, cached answers, logs and backups expire, and which of those deadlines you can verify.
Contract reviewAttach the retention schedule and support-access rules to the procurement record. Assign an owner to follow up on unanswered questions.

Remaining retention obligation

Read the result carefully

An empty search result shows what the user can retrieve at that moment. It cannot establish that a backup expired. Record the retrieval test and the vendor’s retention evidence as separate findings so the person approving the purchase knows which claim each supports.

Have the data owner sign off on the retention exceptions before sending any real contracts.
